channel.title: draft() Blog
channel.description: Short guides on turning what you say into a story people actually read — from the team behind draft().

item.title: Finding a story in "nothing really happened today"
item.description: Even a day with nothing special in it holds a story. Three questions that fish something worth telling out of an ordinary day, with an example.

item.title: How to end on an echo instead of a moral
item.description: When you're tempted to close with "and that's when I realized how precious it is." Three ways to cut the lesson and end on a scene instead, with examples.

item.title: One first line can save a story: how to write a hook
item.description: Posts that open with explanation are hard to finish. Three ways to write a first line that starts in the middle of a scene, with examples.

item.title: A 30-second speaking drill: pick just one scene from today
item.description: If explaining your whole day makes you freeze, pick a single scene instead. A simple drill for pulling the raw material of a story out in thirty seconds.

item.title: Stuck at the blank caption box? Say it out loud instead
item.description: You had a whole day, but the caption box gives you nothing. Here's how to get the story out by talking first, then letting a few questions find the real moment.
